decisions.reason: The question asks for the lowest multiclass 0–1 loss on a fixed discrete dataset under a test-time attacker. The method mentions soft classifiers, but the question does not state the worst-case objective or specify the perturbation model.
The method identifies training examples as vertices and distinct classes as a condition for hyperedges. It does not make clear that all neighborhoods in a hyperedge must share one common point.

The method names the linear program and its purpose but omits the probability-weighted worst-case correctness objective, the nonnegativity and hyperedge-sum constraints, and the exact achievable loss as one minus the maximum.

The figure lists MNIST digits 1, 4, and 7 and CIFAR-10 class IDs 0, 2, and 8. The poster does not name the CIFAR-10 classes or report 1,000 samples per class and the use of the full training sets for the ten-class bounds.
The figure plots 0–1 loss across epsilon values, the result names TRADES, and the caption names APGD. The poster omits the ℓ₂ norm and the APGD-CE and AutoAttack identifiers.
The plots show three-class gaps at small tested budgets, and the headline highlights the CIFAR-10 example. The poster does not discuss the gap relative to the ten-class bounds.

The caption describes the edge-only lower bound for the three-class plots. It does not cover the ten-class truncations through degrees 2, 3, and 4 or the looser maximum-weight coupling bound from pairwise binary optima.
The poster omits the generalized Caro–Wei upper bound for hard and soft classifiers and its observed agreement with the truncated lower bounds at small tested budgets.

The poster omits the computational costs of larger budgets, sample sizes, and class counts, as well as the training-fit interpretation and the open problem of closing the gap while maintaining generalization.

notes: The title and section headings make the reading order clear. Axis labels, ticks, and legends are small, and the headline’s epsilon renders as a white square even though the editable text contains ϵ. The headline gives no numerical budget, so the comparison can only be located approximately from the low-budget end of the CIFAR-10 plot. The plotted values there are consistent with the stated approximations. The square is a rendering defect.
